value: Settle what makes a thing a device in Cairn — the shim FITTED to it and the protocols it answers, not a class it inherits — and derive the base device from the librarian, which Akien names as its template.

value.SUPERSEDED: The three fields below are the numbers this ticket was cast on, kept verbatim because a record of truth is never edited to hide the shape it used to have (Law 7). Two of them are WRONG. Read 'corrected' instead.
value.divergence: The two axes disagree about SIX components: six things inherit device-hood and have no fitted shim. cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py is one of them — which answers the sibling alarms node's central question ('should trouble be a device') by measurement before that node got to ask it.
value.instrument: import_sieve importers_of, run at the design step — not read

value.and_a_third_axis_the_cast_did_not_know_a: Akien RULED a device-ness predicate the same day (2026-08-11, shipped in commit 2081efa): a device is a directory with a probes/ subdirectory, its id the directory's own name. RUN — cairn.devices.ground_loop.discovery.device_folders() over the repo root, not reimplemented — that predicate yields TWELVE: base, bin, design, harbor_master, idea, inference_domain, intent, launchers, learning_block, librarian, saveslate, sorted. Only ONE component is on all three axes: librarian. The symmetric difference between axis 1 and axis 3 is 19 of a 20-member union. ELEVEN Calibre-shaped members already exist — ruled a device, no device class, no shim class — so this ticket's falsifier ('done when a Calibre-shaped member passes') is satisfied eleven times over by code that shipped before the build started. What is absent is not the mechanism; it is anything LOUD about the divergence.
value.corrected_at: 2026-08-11, at the BUILDME step of this ticket's own voyage — piece 1 of the triage order, deliberately AHEAD of every instrument that reads these numbers rather than as bookkeeping at the close.
value.instrument: ast.parse over cairn/**/*.py excluding proofs/ and probes/, collecting every ClassDef's base names — a class census, run, not read.
value.the_method_error: The shim count was a FILENAME census standing in for a CLASS census. I looked for files named shim.py and found three. system_rackmount's shim is the class SystemRackmountShim in cairn/devices/system_rackmount/rackmount.py — a BaseShim subclass that does not live in a file called shim.py, so a filename search cannot see it. This is the author of a ticket about 'a class read is a proxy for a behavioral question' committing the proxy error at his own cast, one field below the sentence naming it. The number was wrong because the INSTRUMENT was wrong; correcting the number without naming the instrument would leave the next census free to repeat it.
value.what_survives_the_correction: The finding does not change: cairn/devices/trouble still imports BaseDevice and still has no shim, so the sibling alarms node's central question is still answered by measurement. What changes is that system_rackmount moves OFF the diverging list — it has both — and the carrier's starting number is 5, not 6.

value: Does the librarian generalize? It is ONE instance and the most elaborated one, so the template may encode its specifics — graph trees, tenure loop — as though they were universal. The check: extract, then ask what a SECOND device wants from it. Carried openly rather than resolved, because extraction is the only way to test it.
Does BaseShim invert to become the load-bearing class and BaseDevice the optional one? Reasoned to, NOT checked against the spine. Carried as an open question, not a settled claim.

cairn/tools/base/intention+why.json — record the collision at BOTH ends. Base's charter asserts 'a value carried by a class you cannot subclass without is physics (Law 4)'; that claim to define device-ness ends here. Its real why — the UNIFORM INTROSPECTION SURFACE, 'the tester probes one protocol, the web UI renders one protocol' — survives intact and is the same axis Akien named. Inheritance was the delivery mechanism, not the value. The edit is part of this ticket's deliverable, not a follow-up someone remembers: a collision recorded only on the newcomer leaves the older artifact still asserting what we stopped believing (Law 5).

runtime-role-is-a-second-axis — cast from the same conversation; rules whether runtime role is an axis at all. Recorded ruling order: THIS TICKET first (it defines what 'device' MEANS), then the axis ticket, then alarms.

every-device-has-a-presence — cast 2026-08-11, downstream-compatible: 'every device has a PRESENCE — an always-on shim', with shims resident in process 2. Its child the-shim-declares-its-device-contract is claimed here.

Filled at the PROVED crossing, which is when a real crossing needed it (the field is deliberately not back-filled — a value nobody checked is a guess with confidence attached). cairn/tools/base and not ground_loop, though ground_loop owns the discovery mechanism the ruling created: this voyage did not build that mechanism — it shipped in 2081efa before the ticket opened. What this voyage changed is base's — BaseDevice's claim to DEFINE device-ness, the predicate that replaces it (cairn/tools/base/deviceness.py), and the probe that makes the divergence loud, which berths at cairn/tools/base/probes/ because that is what it watches. Every crossing on this ticket is journaled in cairn/tools/base/history.json, so intent, voyage and proofs already share that address (Law 5); naming a different owner here would split them.
